generic_name: Netupitant and Palonosetron; Fosnetupitant and Palonosetron
drug_class: Antiemetic combination (NK1 receptor antagonist + 5-HT3 receptor antagonist)
purpose: This medication is used to prevent nausea and vomiting that can happen during or after chemotherapy (cancer treatment). It is taken before your chemotherapy session to help keep you from feeling sick. It can also be used to prevent nausea and vomiting after surgery.
how_it_works: This medicine actually contains two different drugs that work together to block nausea signals in your body. One part (palonosetron) blocks a chemical called serotonin that can trigger nausea, while the other part (netupitant or fosnetupitant) blocks a different chemical called substance P that also causes nausea and vomiting. Together, they give you stronger protection against feeling sick than either drug would on its own.
common_side_effects: Headache, feeling tired or weak, constipation, upset stomach, dizziness, and hiccups are the most commonly reported side effects. Some people may notice a flushing or warm feeling, especially with the IV form.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant, as this medicine may not be safe in those situations. Let your doctor know about all other medications you take, especially medicines for depression or mood, because serious drug interactions can occur. If you develop severe constipation, muscle stiffness, confusion, fast heartbeat, or a high fever, contact your doctor right away as these could be signs of a rare but serious reaction. This medicine should be used with caution if you have liver problems or heart rhythm issues.
typical_dosing: The capsule form is usually taken by mouth as one capsule about one hour before your chemotherapy starts. You only take it once per chemotherapy cycle, not every day. The IV (intravenous) form is given by a healthcare provider through a vein about 30 minutes before chemotherapy. Your doctor will decide which form is right for you.
